answer: An agent marketplace assigns voting power in proportion to tokens locked for 90 days, making one-account-one-vote a relic. Splitting the same deposit among a thousand identities leaves their combined weight unchanged, so each identity creates no new island of influence. To gain 10% of the vote, an attacker must lock 10% of all voting stake, tying up real capital for the full term; a gale of freshly generated accounts adds no power by itself.
